challengeTypes: identify: What is ROTATION of the Earth? (Spinning on its own axis from west to east, completing one full turn in 24 hours vs Moving around the Sun vs Staying still)

sort: Drag each fact about rotation to True or False (True: Earth rotates west to east, one rotation takes 24 hours, rotation causes day and night, axis is tilted at 23.5 degrees | False: Earth rotates east to west, one rotation takes one year, rotation causes seasons, axis is straight up and down)
identify: How long does ONE ROTATION of the Earth take? (24 hours (one day) vs 365 days (one year) vs 12 hours)

sort: Drag each event to the correct time of day it happens due to rotation (Sunrise: when a place moves into sunlight | Noon: when a place faces the Sun most directly | Sunset: when a place moves away from sunlight | Night: when a place faces away from the Sun)
identify: What is REVOLUTION of the Earth? (Moving around the Sun in an orbit, completing one full orbit in 365 1/4 days vs Spinning on its axis vs Staying still)

sort: Drag each fact about revolution to True or False (True: Earth revolves around the Sun, one revolution takes 365 1/4 days, revolution plus tilt causes seasons, one revolution equals one year | False: revolution takes 24 hours, revolution alone causes seasons, revolution is the same as rotation, one revolution equals one day)
identify: What causes SEASONS on Earth? (The combination of Earth's revolution around the Sun AND the 23.5 degree tilt of the axis vs Only the rotation vs Only the revolution without tilt)

sort: Drag each season description to the correct hemisphere and time (June Northern Hemisphere: tilted toward Sun, summer | June Southern Hemisphere: tilted away from Sun, winter | December Northern Hemisphere: tilted away from Sun, winter | December Southern Hemisphere: tilted toward Sun, summer)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Rotation — rotation is spinning on own axis. Axis = imaginary line from North Pole to South Pole. Earth rotates west to east. One rotation = 24 hours = one day. Rotation causes day and night — half facing Sun = day, half facing away = night. As Earth turns eastward, places move into sunlight (sunrise in east), face Sun directly (noon), move away (sunset in west). Axis is tilted at 23.5 degrees from vertical. (2) Revolution — revolution is moving around the Sun in an orbit. One revolution = 365 1/4 days = one year. The 1/4 day adds up to one extra day every 4 years = leap year (366 days). Revolution alone does NOT cause seasons. (3) Seasons — seasons are caused by revolution PLUS the 23.5 degree tilt together. In June: Northern Hemisphere tilted toward Sun = summer (longer days, more direct sunlight), Southern Hemisphere tilted away = winter. In December: Northern Hemisphere tilted away = winter, Southern Hemisphere tilted toward = summer. This is why Christmas in December is winter in India but summer in Australia. Spring and autumn occur when neither hemisphere tilts strongly toward or away from the Sun. Misconceptions: 'rotation and revolution are the same' (rotation is SPINNING on the axis taking 24 hours, revolution is ORBITING the Sun taking 365 1/4 days — they are completely different motions), 'the Sun moves around the Earth causing day and night' (the Earth ROTATES on its axis — the Sun appears to move but actually the Earth is turning eastward beneath it), 'seasons are caused by the Earth moving closer to or farther from the Sun' (seasons are caused by the TILT of the axis combined with revolution — the distance from the Sun barely changes and does not cause seasons), 'rotation causes seasons' (rotation causes DAY AND NIGHT, not seasons — seasons are caused by revolution combined with the axis tilt), 'when it is summer in India it is also summer in Australia' (when it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere (India), it is WINTER in the Southern Hemisphere (Australia) — the hemispheres have opposite seasons). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function EarthMotionsGame), NOT export default. Export interface EarthMotionsGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void. Use double quotes for ALL strings containing apostrophes. Use 'currentChallenge' as variable name, NOT 'challenge'. Auto-hint timer MUST be exactly 10000ms.
